01 / LIVE RETIMING

Drag markers.
Retime live.

Spread two markers apart to slow a moment down. Bring them closer to speed it up. The keys between them follow along in real time.

  • Double-click or Ctrl+Click to place a marker.
  • Drag a span bar to move an entire segment.
  • Shift+Click to select markers, then drag a selected marker.

With just one marker, dragging shifts all included editable curves in time. Outside smooth zones, keys beyond the outer markers follow the nearest outer marker’s offset.

02 / EASE CONTROLS

A little ease.
A lot more character.

The blue diamond places the halfway point of the motion exactly where you want it. The two handles shape each side independently.

  • Pull outward for an ease in or ease out.
  • Pull inward for a fast start or fast end.
  • See the affected section and its live percentage.

The controls return to neutral when you release; the timing change stays. Zoom in on short spans to reveal the handles.

03 / SMOOTH ZONES

Keep the rhythm.
Lose the jolt.

A sudden speed change can feel like a sudden stop. Give it room to breathe with a green smooth zone around the marker.

  • Widen the zone to round off the speed change.
  • Smooth your most recent retime live.
  • Press S to auto-smooth every marker.

Smooth zones change nearby key timing. Marker guides stay exactly where you drop them.

04 / ROOM TO EXPERIMENT

Try the what-if.
Keep the good stuff.

Chase a better rhythm without committing to every drag. Step backward and forward through your retimes until it feels right.

  • Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo retime drags.
  • Release your drag, then Enter keeps one Blender undo step.
  • Esc restores your starting animation and exits.

Try Retime, Undo, and Redo in the illustration. In Blender, right-click during a drag cancels that drag; inserted keys stay in retime history too.

The useful details

Before you
hit Retime.

A few answers to get you moving.

Ready to try it?
Which Blender versions does it work with?
Retime Tool requires Blender 5.2 or newer. It works in both the Graph Editor and the Dope Sheet. The current extension version is 2.4.2.
How do I install it?
Download the extension ZIP from Superhive, then drag and drop the ZIP into Blender and confirm the installation. It’s a Blender Extension, so keep the ZIP as downloaded. Start it from the Retime button in either editor’s header or the sidebar tab.
Which curves will it retime?
Every editable, unlocked curve shown in the editor. Use Blender’s visibility filters, such as Only Show Selected, to choose what is included. Enable Selected Curves Only to narrow the scope further. All keys on the included curves are retimed, whether or not the keys themselves are selected.
How do undo, Enter, and Esc work?

Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z step back and forward through retime drags, including keys inserted at markers. Right-click during a drag cancels only that drag.

Release your drag, then press Enter to keep your changes and exit, adding one step to Blender’s normal undo history. Esc resets the animation to how it was when you started, then exits. Retime markers belong to the active session and disappear when you exit.

Will my keys stay on whole frames?
Keys can land on subframes and are not rounded. Snap Markers on Frame is on by default: it places new markers on whole frames and moves dragged markers in whole-frame increments. A marker placed on a subframe can keep that fractional offset if you turn snapping on later. Turn snapping off when you want subframe marker movement.
What should I know about smoothing?

Smooth zones round off speed changes by adjusting nearby key timing. The marker guide stays exactly where you dropped it, while the keyed moment near it can shift. Wide zones and large speed changes can move that key timing by more than one frame.

Adjusting a zone smooths the most recently completed retime live. Each new retime becomes the new smoothing target. After undo, redo, or inserting new keys, the saved zones apply to your next retime instead. If you add or remove markers, complete another retime before adjusting the zones. Press S or use the sidebar to auto-smooth all markers.

Why can’t I see the ease handles?
Ease handles need a span of about 60 pixels on screen to appear. Zoom in on a short span to give the handles enough space.
What does the GPL license mean for buyers?
The extension is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later, an open-source software license. Read the GNU GPL license for the full terms, including the permissions and conditions for using, modifying, and sharing the extension.
